SCANNED: 2026-08-30

=== LOCAL AI AGENT DISCOVERY (Defender for Endpoint, Preview) ===
Defender automatically discovers supported local AI agents AND MCP server configurations (local and remote) on
onboarded Windows and macOS devices. Agent identity = (user, device, agent type). Claude Code in 15 project folders
for one user on one device = ONE inventory entry.
Surfaces: Local AI agent inventory (device + user associations, discovery metadata); Exposure map (relationships
between local AI agents, devices, identities and the resources those identities can reach); Advanced hunting (KQL).
SUPPORTED LOCAL AI AGENTS (enumerated taxonomy):
  CLI agents: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Junie CLI, Kiro CLI, OpenCode, Warp,
              Antigravity CLI
  Desktop apps: ChatGPT Desktop, Claude Desktop, Codex Desktop, Goose Desktop, Hermes Agent, Ollama Desktop,
              Perplexity Desktop, Poe Desktop
  Agentic IDEs: Cursor, Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf), Kiro IDE, Antigravity IDE
  VS Code extensions: Claude Code, Cline, Codex, Gemini Code Assist, GitHub Copilot, Roo Code
  Claw-based agents: OpenClaw, Clawpilot, QClaw, Claw/Nanobot

=== AI AGENT RUNTIME PROTECTION (Defender for Endpoint, Preview) ===
Device-level prompt-injection detection and blocking for local AI agents. Inspects three points in the agent loop:
user prompt, pre-tool call (before execution), post-tool response.
TWO INSPECTION METHODS, each with Disabled / Audit / Block modes:
 1. Agent-native event inspection - `Set-MpPreference -AiAgentProtection <mode>` - uses vendor-supported agent
    event/hook interfaces. Supported agents and their hook docs:
      Claude Code        -> code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks
      Codex CLI          -> developers.openai.com/codex/hooks
      GitHub Copilot CLI -> docs.github.com/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/use-hooks
      GitHub Copilot app -> docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-reference
 2. Network inspection - `Set-MpPreference -AiAgentNetworkInspection <mode>` - inspects agent-to-LLM network flows
    in transit for agents with no vendor event interface.
    DOCUMENTED BYPASS: "Network inspection doesn't support agents that use certificate pinning or HTTP/3."
Requires Defender for Endpoint P2 / M365 E5 / Microsoft Agent 365 / M365 E7; Defender AV active mode; signature
version 1.451.224.0 or later. NO native Intune policy support - deploy via PowerShell platform scripts in system
context. Setting is protected by tamper protection.
Alert: "Suspicious AI prompt injection". Block mode -> Critical/High/Medium/Low by risk; Audit mode -> Informational.
User sees a block message in the agent terminal plus a Windows toast; also in Windows Security > Protection history.

=== SECURITY FOR AI (Defender XDR) ===
Enabled automatically when a tenant onboards to Microsoft Agent 365 ("Enable" toggle ON by default).
Setup: Settings > Security for AI > Get started. Data sources: Agent 365 (auto Done), Microsoft 365 connector
(requires Entra ID Management events + Microsoft 365 activities; Entra Users and groups is a prerequisite),
Copilot Studio real-time protection (requires a Power Platform admin and a shared Entra App ID).
CLOUD/PLATFORM AGENT DISCOVERY spans Microsoft Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry, AWS Bedrock and GCP Vertex AI,
plus M365 Copilot Agent Builder and non-Microsoft agents built with the Microsoft Agent 365 SDK.
Posture: Advanced Hunting prebuilt queries for misconfigurations, risky agent settings, excessive permissions.
Threat detection scenarios: indirect prompt injection, evasion techniques, malicious content propagation, secret
leakage, LLM reconnaissance, suspicious IP access.

=== REAL-TIME PROTECTION RULES (Defender XDR) ===
Coverage by agent type:
  - Agent 365 tool invocations: via Work IQ MCP, including customer MCP tools onboarded to Agent 365. Agents that
    rely on unsupported tools or don't integrate with Work IQ MCP ARE NOT COVERED.
  - Copilot Studio agents (Preview): evaluates tool invocations, independent of Work IQ MCP.
  - Foundry agents (Preview): evaluates user requests, agent responses, tool invocations AND tool responses.
  - Local AI agents: via Defender for Endpoint runtime protection.
Rule types: built-in Default rule audits ALL agents (records behaviour, does not stop); Custom rules block matching
actions and record the behaviour, scoped to All agents or specific agents, with an Exclude list.
IMPORTANT: the agent Exclude picker only lists "agents with a Microsoft Entra agent ID."
Detection types selectable on a rule: Secret exfiltration, Malicious content propagation, Evasion techniques,
Unsafe email domain.
Audited and blocked activity is recorded as behaviours in the `BehaviorInfo` table (what happened, why it was
risky, which agent/user/tool). Near-real-time detections surface as alerts ONLY in audit mode - when a blocking
rule covers an agent, near-real-time alerts are NOT generated for that agent.
Prompt Shields block events for Foundry and M365 Copilot Agent Builder are also recorded as behaviours; NOT yet
supported for Copilot Studio agents.
Prompt evidence collection (Settings > Security for AI > Prompt evidence collection) includes user prompt / agent
response snippets as alert evidence, on by default, secrets redacted.

=== COPILOT STUDIO EXTERNAL THREAT DETECTION PROVIDER (Preview) ===
"Bring your own protection." Every time the orchestrator considers invoking a tool it POSTs the proposed tool use
to an external REST endpoint which returns allow or block.
Only called on GENERATIVE agents using generative orchestration; SKIPPED for classic agents.
API (api-version=2025-05-01), two endpoints:
  POST /validate                 - health/readiness check. Response {isSuccessful, status}.
  POST /analyze-tool-execution   - risk evaluation. Response {blockAction, reasonCode?, reason?, diagnostics?}.
Request body (EvaluationRequest):
  plannerContext   - userMessage, thought (planner's reasoning for tool choice), chatHistory[] (id/role/content/
                     timestamp), previousToolOutputs[] (toolId, toolName, outputs with values, timestamp)
  toolDefinition   - id, type, name, description, inputParameters[], outputParameters[]
  inputValues      - the actual key/value arguments about to be passed to the tool
  conversationMetadata - agent {id, tenantId, environmentId, version, isPublished}, user {Entra oid, tenantId},
                     trigger {id, schemaName}, conversationId, planId, planStepId, parentAgentComponentId
Auth: Entra ID; Federated Identity Credentials (secret-less), explicit subject identifier
  /eid1/c/pub/t/{b64 tenantId}/a/m1WPnYRZpEaQKq1Cceg--g/{b64 endpoint}
  Setup via Create-CopilotWebhookApp.ps1 (PowerShell Gallery) or manual Azure portal registration.
Configured in Power Platform admin center > Security > Threat detection > Additional threat detection.
FAIL-OPEN BY DEFAULT: response required in <1000 ms; "If your system doesn't respond in time, the agent behaves as
if your response is 'allow', invoking the tool." Error behaviour is configurable to "Block the query".
NO TENANT-WIDE SETTING: "There's no PowerShell, API, or admin center setting to enforce or propagate this
configuration globally"; must be turned on manually PER ENVIRONMENT, including every newly created environment.
Named provider option: Microsoft Defender (defender-cloud-apps/real-time-agent-protection-during-runtime), custom
in-house systems, or "products from other trusted security providers".
Provider receives data that "might be processed and stored outside your geographic region".
